newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - May 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - May 20.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- President Nelson Mandela lashed out on Monday at critics of Laurent Kabila's new regimein Zaire when he became the first South African leader to address the Zimbabwean parliament.
- The Presidential Review Commission, set up to achieve a fundamental overhaul of the public service, had done no work for six months and would have to be resurrected, parliament was told on Monday.
- JCI Ltd's talks on a potential merger with Lonrho Plc could be scuttled as mining houses Avmin Ltd and Gencor Ltd become serious contenders in linking up with the UK conglomerate, sources said.

- Renewed conflict looms at Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd (Amplats) mine's Rustenburg section as tension mounted on Monday between the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) and the Worker Mouthpiece, a worker grouping which led last year's lengthy strike.

- Brownwyn Keene-Young, the head of the Independent Broadcasting Authority's monitoring and complaints department, was appointed acting CEO on Monday, and accounting firm Deloitte & Touche was asked to take over the finance and administration.
BUSINESS REPORT

- The payment of bribes, or "payola", to disc jockeys and radio station programmers to influence the playing of records was rife in the South African music industry, Michael Edwards, the former managing director of EMI South Africa, has told the industrial court.

- Barlow Ltd the diversified heavy industrial group, was left nursing lower margins on its domestic operations after a downturn in capital spending in the South African economy, the company said on Monday.
- The gold price came under pressure on Monday as negative sentiment returned to the bullion market after the German central bank announced last week it was revaluing its reserves.

- Allegations of fraud, insider trading and reckless trading against five former directors of Crusader Life Ltd, the life assurer, were being investigated, the Office for Serious Economic Offences said on Monday.
- Unifruco, the fruit exporting body, said on Monday it had dumped 100,000 cartons of plums in Europe earlier this year.
SAKE BEELD
- The Office for Serious Economic Offences has placed a moratorium on new cases indefinitely due to a shortage of legally qualified staff.
- Transnet has begun an inquiry into the payment of 12,000 rand by Portnet's legal chief Themba Mthethwa to Enoch Sithole, communications director at the SABC.
- Up to 50,000 bank workers pledge to participate in a march on Thursday in protest against the spate of armed robberies.
THE STAR
- New moves against car thieves and hijackers are to be introduced following the compilation of the most detailed report yet produced on the blight, estimated to cost about six billion rand a year.

- Democratic Republic of Congo leader Laurent Kabila would peacefully enter Kinshasa on Tuesday, four days after rebel troops seized the country's capital, South African President Nelson Mandela said on Monday.
- A reward of 250,000 rand is being offered for a man wanted in connection with the shooting of well-known Johannesburg horse trainer David Ferraris last year.

- Top black National Party MP David Chuenyane has called for the resignation of the NP leadership, including F.W. de Klerk, for failing to transform itself by appointing black Nats to decision-making positions.

- South Africa's Thabo Mbeki and Desmond Tutu on Monday made passionate appeals for all African states to join forces to unearth an estimated 50 million landmines buried on the continent and to approve a total ban on these "indiscriminate killers".
